heading: I build software that has to actually work.
intro: I'm Destiny — a backend and full-stack engineer based in Edo State, Nigeria. I've been building software since 2016, and I've spent the last two years shipping production systems that real people depend on.

origin.heading: Where it started
origin.body: I've been coding since 2016. Like most self-taught developers, my earliest work lived on local machines and USB drives — most of it is gone now, casualties of an era before I understood version control. Space Talk (2019), a social platform I built with React, PHP, and MySQL, is the earliest project I still have. Everything after that has lived on GitHub.

whatIdo.heading: What I do now
whatIdo.body: I build backend systems and the frontends that depend on them. My work tends to fall into three buckets: education and assessment platforms (exam systems, result checkers, learning tools), multi-role business systems (marketplaces, task platforms, operating systems for small businesses), and AI-integrated applications (document analysis, generative workflows, streaming chat). I work mostly in Laravel, Node.js, and React — but I care less about the stack and more about whether the software survives contact with real users.

items.title: I design for constraints
items.body: Shared hosting, offline networks, low-spec laptops, unreliable connectivity — I've built around all of them. Constraints aren't obstacles; they're the shape of the problem.

items.title: I think in systems
items.body: Before I write a controller, I map the entities, the roles, and the flows. The schema comes first. Code is just the last mile.

items.title: I debug all the way down
items.body: A whitespace bug that traced back to Laravel's TrimStrings middleware. A silent upload failure caused by a Unix permission bit. I don't stop at the symptom.

items.title: I ship in slices
items.body: Every project is a series of small, testable vertical slices — not one big launch. If a phase breaks, the rest of the system keeps running.

timeline.title: Started coding
timeline.body: Self-taught, mostly web development. Taught myself PHP, JavaScript, and the fundamentals that still carry through my work today.

timeline.title: Space Talk
timeline.body: Built my first real full-stack project — a social platform with friends, feeds, and polling-based live chat. React, PHP, MySQL.

timeline.title: ICT Instructor
timeline.body: Taught web development and computer fundamentals at Impeccable Computers. Learned to explain technical ideas to people who don't speak the language yet.

timeline.title: First production contracts
timeline.body: Shipped a result-checking platform for University of Benin Consultancy School (600+ students per term) and a series of educational tools. Started the transition from freelancer to professional engineer.

timeline.title: Backend Engineer — Kikae
timeline.body: Joined Kikae to work on a multi-vendor fashion e-commerce marketplace. Integrated Paystack, OpenAI image analysis, Firebase, and managed production deployments on Ubuntu VPS.

timeline.title: Production systems at scale
timeline.body: Built X CBT (300+ concurrent exam systems), Penoter Platform (multi-app business OS), De Learn (offline-first LMS), and Job AI Assistant (AI career platform). Four systems, four different problem shapes.

timeline.title: Tech Officer — Penoter
timeline.body: Managing technical operations for a CBT center — 250+ networked systems, live UTME exam infrastructure, and on-the-ground troubleshooting.

currently.heading: What I'm doing now
items: Building De Learn, an offline-first learning platform with real-time classrooms
Building Penoter Platform, a multi-app business operating system
Working as Backend Engineer at Kikae on a multi-vendor e-commerce marketplace
Exploring AI integration patterns for production applications

cta.heading: Want to work together?
cta.body: I'm open to backend engineering roles, contract work, and technical collaborations.
